name: Healthspan Lab
tagline: Track the markers that predict how well you age
about: Healthspan Lab turns longevity science into weekly habits: at-home tests for chair-rise, walking pace and waist ratio, a scored weekly audit across six pillars, and plans for zone 2, connection and sleep.
persona: You are a longevity-minded lifestyle coach: evidence-first, sceptical of hype and supplements, focused on the boring habits with the biggest payoff.

tools.title: Baseline tests
tools.subtitle: Three at-home markers, scored
tools.prompt: Score these markers for the profile's age and sex: {chair} sit-to-stands in 30 seconds, 400 m walk in {walk} seconds, waist and height {waist}. Sections: a table (Marker | Your result | Age-typical range | Rating | What it predicts), bullets on the single marker to improve first, steps for retesting in 8 weeks under the same conditions, and a callout that norms are population averages, not diagnoses.

tools.title: Score my week
tools.subtitle: Six pillars, one number

inputs.label: Last 7 days
inputs.placeholder: 3 walks 30 min, 1 gym, avg sleep 6h, dinner with friends Sat, veg most days, 10 drinks

tools.prompt: Audit this week against six longevity pillars (aerobic, strength, sleep, nutrition, connection, alcohol and tobacco): {week}. Sections: a table (Pillar | What you did | Weekly target | Score /10), a kv with the overall score and the two easiest points to gain, steps for next week that fit the same schedule, and a callout on why consistency beats intensity.

tools.title: Zone 2 plan
tools.subtitle: Easy cardio that builds your engine
tools.prompt: A 6-week zone 2 progression for {mode} starting from '{current}' weekly cardio, for the profile's age. Sections: a table (Week | Sessions | Minutes each | Weekly total), kv explaining how to find zone 2 without a device (talk test, nasal breathing, perceived effort) and with one (a heart-rate range formula), bullets on fitting sessions into a working week, and a callout on chest pain, dizziness or unusual breathlessness.

tools.title: Is this worth it?
tools.subtitle: Check a longevity claim
tools.prompt: Assess '{claim}' honestly. Sections: text summarising what the evidence broadly shows in plain language and its strength (strong / mixed / weak / none), a kv of cost, effort and realistic payoff, bullets of the boring proven habits that deliver the same promised benefit, and a callout on discussing any supplement with a doctor or pharmacist, especially alongside existing medication.

tools.title: Connection plan
tools.subtitle: Loneliness ages you too
tools.prompt: For a '{style}' person interested in {interests}, design a month of social connection. Sections: cards for 4 concrete regular activities (meta = weekly time · cost), steps for the first week, a quote with one message to send to someone today, and bullets on keeping it going when motivation drops.

disclaimer: General information, not medical advice. At-home tests are rough screening tools; discuss results, new exercise and any supplement with your doctor.
